# StatCite — complete reference for AI agents

StatCite serves official economic statistics with full citations. Free, no auth, read-only.

- MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP, stateless, protocol 2025-03-26/2025-06-18/2025-11-25): https://statcite.com/mcp
- REST base: https://statcite.com/v1  (OpenAPI: https://statcite.com/openapi.json)
- Every numeric response includes a citation object: {source, dataset, series_id, series_name, source_url, api_url, license, attribution, retrieved_at, citation_text, notices?}. Reproduce citation_text when presenting numbers to users.
- Data sources: World Bank WDI (CC BY 4.0), IMF WEO/Fiscal Monitor via the IMF DataMapper API — current vintage, DBnomics as a vintage-pinned fallback (attribution: "Source: International Monetary Fund"), ECB euro reference rates via Frankfurter. FRED is permanently disabled — its terms of use prohibit AI/ML use and caching/redistribution of its content, which conflicts with this service's architecture; the fred/… series id and six US-only registry keys are recognized but always decline.
- IMF forward-year values are labeled as estimates/projections per-observation; "latest" prefers the latest value not marked as a projection (which may itself be a staff estimate — the IMF's true latest-actual year varies by country). The projection boundary is a heuristic derived from each response's own data horizon, not a per-country authoritative cutoff (some earlier observations may also be staff estimates — notes say so; a series ending before the boundary year gets an explicit note). Citations pass through the IMF's own verbatim edition label; any fallback carries an explicit disclosure, and verify_stat/verify_claims return cannot_verify rather than a match/mismatch verdict whenever the served value came from a transient-failure fallback, since substitutes can differ by definition (World Bank vs IMF) or vintage by far more than rounding for identical historical years; a fallback for a series the primary permanently lacks is judged normally with disclosure.
- Statistics get revised: values reflect the source's currently published figure.

## MCP tools

### get_indicator
Official values for a curated indicator, any country.
Args: indicator (registry key, required), country (ISO3/ISO2/name, required), start_year?, end_year?, transform? (none|yoy|pct_change|index), latest_only? (bool), strict_source? (bool — reproducibility mode: if the primary source fails, error instead of serving the fallback source). Fallback-served responses carry fallback_used: true plus a disclosure note naming both sources.
Example: {"indicator":"inflation_cpi","country":"BRB","latest_only":true}

### verify_stat
Check a claimed figure against the official series. THE tool to call before publishing any economic number.
Args: indicator (registry key or explicit series id), country?, period (usually "YYYY"; quarters as "YYYY-Qn"/"YYYYQn"/"YYYY Qn", months as "YYYY-MM"/"YYYYMM"), claimed_value (number), tolerance_abs?, tolerance_pct?, strict_source? (bool — never verify against a fallback source; error instead), as_of? (date, e.g. "2019-04" — historical IMF-vintage verification: judge against a dated IMF WEO edition instead of today's data; only for gdp_growth, current_account_gdp, govt_debt_gdp, fiscal_balance_gdp, govt_revenue_gdp, govt_expenditure_gdp; impossible calendar dates are rejected).
Returns verdict: match | close | mismatch | cannot_verify, plus official_value, difference, is_projection (true when the matched official observation is an IMF WEO/Fiscal Monitor estimate/projection, with the explanation qualified accordingly), observation_status (actual | modeled_estimate | estimate_or_actual | projection | unknown — "modeled_estimate" means the registry flags the series as a modeled publication, e.g. ILO-modeled unemployment: a published figure but a model output, never an outturn; "estimate_or_actual" means an IMF observation before the projection boundary, which may still be a staff estimate, never a confirmed actual; "unknown" also covers explicit series ids StatCite doesn't classify, which can be forecast datasets), status_method (horizon_heuristic for IMF series, as_published otherwise), diagnostics (year misattribution, percent-vs-decimal, scale confusion up to 10^12, sign flips), citation, as_of ({requested, resolved_vintage, resolution, verification_scope, normal_primary_source, source_changed_for_as_of} — present only when as_of was used; see the historical-verification paragraph below). A registry verify served from a transient-failure fallback returns cannot_verify with the fallback value as indicative (fallback_used: true) — substitutes can differ by definition or vintage beyond the verdict bands, and the primary may recover and serve a different number. When the primary permanently lacks the series/country (e.g. Taiwan in WDI), the fallback is the stable serving source and the verdict is judged normally with disclosure.
Default thresholds: percent-kind series → match ≤0.06pp or ≤0.5% rel, close ≤0.3pp or ≤2% rel; levels → match ≤0.5% rel, close ≤5% rel.
Historical IMF-vintage verification (as_of): judges the claim against a dated IMF WEO edition — NOT exact "truth at the time". Two disclosed bounds: (1) the vintage is resolved with a CONSERVATIVE month calendar (editions flip May 1 / Nov 1, not the IMF's actual release days — a date inside a release month resolves to the previous edition even if the new one already existed; the response's as_of.resolution and a note say so, and get_series with a dated dbnomics/IMF/WEO:YYYY-MM id pins exactly); (2) as_of always verifies against the WEO archive even when the indicator's live primary is World Bank WDI or the IMF Fiscal Monitor — as_of.source_changed_for_as_of flags this, since a claim from the live primary can differ from WEO for methodological reasons, not only revisions. Dated editions confirmed back to at least 2010-04. Rejects with advice for indicators/ids with no dated vintage. Full as_of response object: {requested, resolved_vintage, resolution, verification_scope, normal_primary_source, source_changed_for_as_of}.

### verify_claims
Batch fact-check: verify a whole draft's macro claims in one call instead of one verify_stat call each. Extract every checkable claim (indicator + country + period + claimed value) from the text, then submit them together.
Args: claims — array of 1–15 objects, each {indicator, country?, period, claimed_value, tolerance_abs?, tolerance_pct?, as_of?} (same fields as verify_stat); optional call-level strict_source? (bool) applies reproducibility mode to every claim. Max 15 per call (free-tier subrequest budget); split larger drafts into batches.
Returns: {summary, results, note?}.
- summary: {total, match, close, mismatch, cannot_verify, error} — verdict counts across the batch.
- results: in input order; each item is {ok:true, claim, verification} where verification is the full verify_stat payload (verdict, official_value, difference, diagnostics, is_projection, citation) — or {ok:false, claim, error} when that claim could not be resolved (unknown indicator/country, upstream trouble). Per-claim errors never sink the rest of the batch; they count under summary.error.
- note: present when some claims were verified against IMF WEO/Fiscal Monitor projection-period observations (pre-boundary values are "estimate_or_actual", not confirmed outturns).
REST: POST /v1/verify_claims with JSON body {"claims":[...]} — the API's only non-GET route. GET → 405 advice; non-JSON content-type → 415; malformed body → 422.

### get_series
Raw series by explicit id: "worldbank/<WDI code>" (+country), "imf/<CODE>" (+country; current-vintage IMF WEO/Fiscal Monitor via DataMapper, e.g. "imf/NGDP_RPCH"), "dbnomics/<PROVIDER>/<DATASET>/<SERIES>" e.g. "dbnomics/IMF/WEO:latest/BRB.NGDP_RPCH.pcent_change" (a dated edition like "WEO:2025-04" pins an exact vintage for reproducibility). "fred/<ID>" is recognized but always declines — FRED is permanently disabled.
Args: series_id, country?, start_year?, end_year?, transform?.

### search_indicators
Free-text search over the registry + DBnomics dataset discovery. Args: query. Indicator results carry active (boolean) — a disabled FRED-reserved key says so in its description and usage ("do not call") instead of pretending to be fetchable.

### country_snapshot
11 headline indicators for one country, each with its own citation. Args: country.

### inflation_adjust
Args: amount, from_year, to_year, country? (default USA). CPI-ratio method (World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL), formula disclosed. Annual-average precision.

### fx_convert
Args: amount, from, to (ISO 4217), date? ("YYYY-MM-DD" daily | "YYYY" annual | omit=latest).
ECB daily reference rates for ~30 majors since 1999; ~90 more currencies via World Bank official annual-average rates (USD bridge). Response includes precision: daily|annual_average|mixed and the exact method.

### list_sources
Sources, coverage, licenses, required attribution lines.

### search / fetch (deep-research pair)
search({query}) → {results:[{id,title,url}]} with ids like "indicator/inflation_cpi/BRB".
fetch({id}) → {id,title,text,url,metadata}; text contains recent observations + full citation.

## REST endpoints (GET unless noted)

- /v1 — endpoint index
- /v1/indicators — full registry; each entry carries active (boolean) and, on the six permanently-disabled FRED-reserved keys, disabled_reason
- /v1/indicator/{key}?country=&start_year=&end_year=&transform=&latest_only=&strict_source=
- /v1/series?id=&country=&start_year=&end_year=&transform=&strict_source=
- /v1/search?q=
- /v1/snapshot/{country}
- /v1/verify?indicator=&country=&period=&value=&tolerance_abs=&tolerance_pct=&strict_source=&as_of=
- /v1/verify_claims — POST, JSON body {"claims":[...], "strict_source"?: bool}, 1–15 claims (the only non-GET route)
- /v1/inflation?amount=&from_year=&to_year=&country=
- /v1/fx?amount=&from=&to=&date=
- /v1/sources
- /health

Errors: 400 missing params, 422 helpful failure (suggestions included), 502 upstream trouble. /v1/verify_claims: 405 on GET, 415 on non-JSON content-type, 422 on malformed body.

## Indicator registry (46 keys — 40 active; the six FRED-reserved US keys always decline)

- gdp_growth — GDP growth (annual %) [% (annual, real)] (sources: World Bank WDI; IMF DataMapper API (current WEO/Fiscal Monitor); IMF WEO (via DBnomics))
- gdp_current_usd — GDP (current US$) [current US$] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- gdp_per_capita_usd — GDP per capita (current US$) [current US$] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- gdp_per_capita_ppp — GDP per capita, PPP (current international $) [current international $ (PPP)] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- gni_per_capita_atlas — GNI per capita, Atlas method (current US$) [current US$] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- inflation_cpi — Inflation, consumer prices (annual %) [% (annual average)] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- cpi_index — Consumer price index (2010 = 100) [index, 2010 = 100] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- gdp_deflator_growth — Inflation, GDP deflator (annual %) [%] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- unemployment_rate — Unemployment, total (% of labor force, modeled ILO estimate) [% of labor force] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- labor_force_participation — Labor force participation rate (% of population 15+, modeled ILO) [% of population ages 15+] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- population — Population, total [people] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- population_growth — Population growth (annual %) [%] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- current_account_gdp — Current account balance (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI; IMF DataMapper API (current WEO/Fiscal Monitor); IMF WEO (via DBnomics))
- govt_debt_gdp — General government gross debt (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: IMF DataMapper API (current WEO/Fiscal Monitor); IMF WEO (via DBnomics); World Bank WDI)
- fiscal_balance_gdp — General government net lending/borrowing (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: IMF DataMapper API (current WEO/Fiscal Monitor); IMF WEO (via DBnomics))
- govt_revenue_gdp — General government revenue (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: IMF DataMapper API (current WEO/Fiscal Monitor); IMF WEO (via DBnomics))
- govt_expenditure_gdp — General government total expenditure (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: IMF DataMapper API (current WEO/Fiscal Monitor); IMF WEO (via DBnomics))
- tax_revenue_gdp — Tax revenue (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- trade_gdp — Trade (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- exports_gdp — Exports of goods and services (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- imports_gdp — Imports of goods and services (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- fdi_inflows_gdp — Foreign direct investment, net inflows (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- remittances_gdp — Personal remittances, received (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- gross_capital_formation_gdp — Gross capital formation (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- gross_savings_gdp — Gross savings (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- official_fx_rate — Official exchange rate (LCU per US$, period average) [LCU per US$] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- reserves_months_imports — Total reserves in months of imports [months of imports] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- reserves_total_usd — Total reserves (includes gold, current US$) [current US$] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- lending_rate — Lending interest rate (%) [%] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- deposit_rate — Deposit interest rate (%) [%] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- real_interest_rate — Real interest rate (%) [%] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- broad_money_gdp — Broad money (% of GDP) [% of GDP] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- gini — Gini index [index (0–100)] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- poverty_headcount_intl — Poverty headcount ratio at $2.15/day, 2017 PPP (% of population) [% of population] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- life_expectancy — Life expectancy at birth, total (years) [years] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- urban_population_share — Urban population (% of total population) [% of population] (sources: World Bank WDI)
- us_fed_funds_rate — US federal funds effective rate (monthly, %) [%] (sources: FRED (US) — disabled, always declines)
- us_10y_treasury — US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield (daily, %) [%] (sources: FRED (US) — disabled, always declines)
- us_cpi_monthly — US CPI for all urban consumers (monthly index, 1982–84 = 100) [index, 1982–84 = 100] (sources: FRED (US) — disabled, always declines)
- us_unemployment_monthly — US unemployment rate (monthly, %) [%] (sources: FRED (US) — disabled, always declines)
- us_nonfarm_payrolls — US total nonfarm payrolls (monthly, thousands of persons) [thousands of persons] (sources: FRED (US) — disabled, always declines)
- us_real_gdp — US real GDP (quarterly, chained 2017 dollars, SAAR) [billions of chained 2017 US$] (sources: FRED (US) — disabled, always declines)

## Countries
ISO3/ISO2 codes or English names; aliases resolve (UK, South Korea, Ivory Coast, Türkiye…). Aggregates: WLD, EUU, EMU, OED, HIC/LIC/LMC/UMC, regions (LCN, SSF, EAS, ECS, MEA, NAC, SAS).

## Fair use
Free, no key. Cache-friendly; keep sustained automated load reasonable. Metered alternative: "StatCite — Economic Data & Stat Verification" on Apify (https://apify.com/asokore/statcite-economic-data). Contact: hello@statcite.com
